description: How a technology name cvENGINE detects reaches the vendor:product a CVE record uses (read by cveFeed.correlation; measured by cveFeed.tech_coverage, manage.py technology_coverage). Every entry names its evidence: the NVD CPE and/or the CVE whose record spells the product that way. 'aliases': a detected name (normalized like correlation normalizes it: case and punctuation dropped) also names these products, and only when the record's vendor is one of 'vendors' (a record with no vendor, or 'n/a', is not contradicted by an exact product). A target is matched exactly, and also by correlation's name rules when the record names one of the vendors ('Microsoft Exchange Server' reaches 'Microsoft Exchange Server 2019 Cumulative Update 12'). 'restrict': a name that may only reach these vendors' records ('require_vendor': a record must name one): a bare name another vendor also uses for a different product. 'ambiguous_products': a product two vendors both use: a record that names no vendor never confirms a name for it. 'vendor_renames': spellings of one vendor across renames and acquisitions, read when a CPE's vendor is compared with a record's and when the coverage report counts vendors. Never add an entry that merges two vendors' different products. 'renames': a detector's name for a reading that names another product ('to'), read as that product (correlation.tech_name). 'protocol_versions': names whose stated version is a protocol's or an API's, never the product's: the version is dropped (correlation.stated_version).

evidence: cpe:2.3:a:apache:tomcat (Tomcat's releases are 3.x to 11.x: no 1.1 exists)
CVE-2025-24813 (Apache Software Foundation: Apache Tomcat, 8.5.0 to 11.0.2: a '1.1' sits below every branch it lists)
protocol_versions.note: nmap prints Tomcat's HTTP connector as 'Apache Tomcat/Coyote JSP engine 1.1' and the Server header says 'Apache-Coyote/1.1': '1.1' is the HTTP/1.1 connector (Http11Processor), the same on every Tomcat release, never a Tomcat version. Read as one, it sat below every branch an advisory fixes and was taken as an end-of-life release affected by every Tomcat CVE. The name is still Tomcat (aliases), an unversioned lead, and the release notes, error page or a header give the real version (cvengine_scanner.versions.PROTOCOL_VERSIONS reads the Server header the same way)
